data.content_ref: inline:The problem asks for the single mechanism best explaining why the nighttime UHI gap is larger in some cities than in others. SRC_001 asserts that this mechanism is the absence of evapotranspiration/impervious cover. But this mechanism primarily explains why the city is warmer in absolute terms, not why the gap varies across cities. The claim that 'cities with greater impervious cover... produce a larger nocturnal temperature gap' is contradicted by the target's own countercondition: arid cities sit over naturally low-ET countryside, so the city–rural ET differential is small, yet arid cities often show the largest nocturnal UHI — driven by the rural surface's rapid radiative cooling (high sky view factor), not by the city's loss of latent cooling. By its own stated falsifier, arid cities with large UHI undermine the universality of the ET-deficit explanation, yet the target still presents ET deficit as the single dominant cross-city modulator.
